- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next period; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- If model shows strong upward trend but sentiment is weak or mixed, reduce slope; mean-reversion bias is common in 3–5 day horizon.
- If true outcome is significantly lower than forecast (e.g., >3% below), check if sentiment was bullish recently — if so, model may have overreacted; apply downward correction.
- If true outcome is significantly higher than forecast (e.g., >3% above), sentiment was likely bearish — model may have missed reversal; adjust upward if sentiment turns positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags by 1–3 days; if sentiment is trending, align forecast with sentiment direction, not just historical mean.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33), model tends to drift toward recent mean — avoid overfitting to recent highs/lows; use sentiment as signal for smoothing.
